text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP). The clinical presentation of frequent epistaxis, mucous membrane bleeding, petechiae on the distal extremities, and bruising in a 4-year-old male is highly characteristic of this condition. To confirm the diagnosis, we must check the platelet count. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count (CBC) with platelet count.
